title: Mirai — Autonomous Intelligence Agent
description:
Mirai is a self-hosted intelligence agent I built to solve a problem I had personally: staying current on AI, technology, and venture activity meant reading a large volume of sources with a poor signal-to-noise ratio. The system reads those sources continuously, decides what is actually worth knowing, and delivers a written weekly briefing every Sunday at 08:00 PT via Telegram and email, with real-time alerts for events that cannot wait for the weekly cycle.

I designed the pipeline in five stages: hourly Python scrapers pull from each configured source; an LLM layer parses every item into structured form and discards low-value material; surviving items are clustered and synthesized into sections; a scheduled delivery job composes the finished issue and pushes it out through the Telegram Bot API and email, firing alerts immediately when a high-signal item cannot wait for Sunday; and a FastAPI dashboard renders the current issue alongside the full archive. Inference is split deliberately between a local Llama model served through Ollama for high-volume parsing and Claude Haiku where synthesis quality matters, which is what keeps the system running at roughly $0.41 per week.

The hard part of this problem is judgment, not collection. Deciding what counts as signal, and then explaining why several unrelated-looking items are the same story, is the work, and it is the part I set out to automate. The system has run unattended since May 2026 and I have iterated on output quality against my own daily use of it. Because it runs locally on my own machine rather than as a hosted service, the dashboard is not public; the render embedded here is Issue No. 14.
